## Description
Report the minimum total cost of reaching vertex \(N\) from vertex 1 in a directed graph. Each move follows an edge in its current direction and costs 1. Reversing all edges costs \(X\) and leaves the current vertex unchanged.

## Preconditions
- **PRE-1 (Unverified):** Standard input contains a line with integers \(N\), \(M\), and \(X\), followed by \(M\) lines, each containing an ordered pair of integer endpoints \(u_i, v_i\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified):** \(2 \le N \le 200{,}000\), \(1 \le M \le 200{,}000\), \(1 \le X \le 10^9\), and all endpoints lie in \([1,N]\). Each pair denotes an edge from \(u_i\) to \(v_i\); repeated pairs and self-loops are not excluded.
- **PRE-3 (Unverified):** Vertex \(N\) is reachable from vertex 1 using the permitted operations.

## Postconditions
- **POST-1 (Unverified):** Every candidate operation sequence starts at vertex 1 with the input edge directions and ends on first reaching vertex \(N\). A move changes only the current vertex and costs 1. A reversal changes every edge direction simultaneously, leaves the current vertex unchanged, and costs \(X\). After any even number of reversals the directions match the input; after any odd number they are opposite.
- **POST-2 (Unverified):** Standard output contains only the exact integer minimum of the summed operation costs over all legal sequences. The result is not truncated if it exceeds the 32-bit integer range. Ties between optimal sequences do not change the output.

## Test suggestions
- Under PRE-1–PRE-3, use \(N=2\) with only \(1\to2\), then only \(2\to1\). Expect 1 and \(X+1\), respectively (POST-1, POST-2).
- Use the same graph with two values of \(X\) so that a reversal is optimal in one case but not in the other (POST-1, POST-2).
- Check a graph that forces several reversals and has a known optimum above the 32-bit integer range (POST-1, POST-2).
- Permute edge lines, duplicate an existing edge, or add a self-loop while staying within PRE-1–PRE-3; check that the minimum is unchanged (POST-2).

## Unspecified behavior
Behavior is unspecified for malformed input, values outside the stated constraints, or an unreachable destination. No operation sequence or tie-breaking rule is required.
